items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: I guess he had been frightened to death by Ohman and Arden or something, and he had to have two pianos.

ctx.x: Well, actually we opened in November of '32 and we played on into '33, and we were there when Roosevelt turned the beer on. I remember they had big ads in the paper, "Free beer tonight," you know, and unfortunately our shipment got hijacked and we had a whole room full of people and no beer. But we finished out that engagement there, just a normal thing. And we were there, I think, three or four months. And we had had a -- oh, a CBS wire in there, radio, and we tried to, you know, float the band out on the road…

in with a whole load of newspapers under his arm, you know, and very serious and attentive to everything that was going on, and came over and introduced himself. I think he was writing for The Melody Maker, the English paper, at that time. We had -- we were using all arrangements there in that band, which at the time, we had three trumpets and trombone, we had four brass and we had four saxophones, and believe it or not we had two piano players. The hotel insisted on having two piano players. Well, they had them,…
Do you remember who was in that band, that first band?
